title: Vibrant Roasted Peruvian Fish Stew
description: This roasted Peruvian fish stew is a comforting and flavorful dish featuring katsuramuki-cut fish and tarragon leaves, perfect for a cold evening. It is a pescatarian-friendly option that combines the richness of fish with the brightness of Peruvian spices.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the katsuramuki-cut halibut pieces and cook for 2 minutes on each side, until they are lightly browned.
Add the roasted and chopped Peruvian aji amarillo peppers, fish stock, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cover the Dutch oven and transfer it to the preheated oven.
Roast the stew in the oven for 15 minutes, until the fish is cooked through and the flavors have melded together.
Stir in the fresh tarragon leaves and serve the stew hot.
